description:
Did You Know Trillions of Ghost Particles Pass Through You?

Episode 75 of a daily journey through the universe. 👻
Season 4 finale. Neutrinos: tiny ghost-like particles made in the Sun and in exploding stars. Trillions pass through your body every second without touching anything. How IceCube, buried in the Antarctic ice, catches them.

➡️ Next stop: The Hubble Space Telescope
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #neutrinos #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Right now, trillions of ghost particles are flying straight through your body.
Right now, as you watch this, ghost particles are flying straight through your body.
segments.headline: Ghost particles

segments.text: Trillions of them every second. They're called neutrinos.
Most come from the Sun, made in the nuclear reactions in its core.
segments.headline: Made in the Sun

segments.text: Neutrinos almost never touch anything. They pass through you, through Earth, as if it weren't there. At night, they come up through the ground.
segments.headline: They pass through Earth

segments.text: So how do you catch a ghost? With something enormous.
segments.headline: How to catch a ghost

segments.text: At the South Pole, scientists buried thousands of light sensors deep in the ice, filling a cubic kilometer. It's called IceCube.
segments.headline: IceCube, South Pole

segments.text: Once in a while, a neutrino hits an atom in the ice and makes a tiny flash of blue light. The sensors catch it.
segments.headline: A tiny blue flash

segments.text: In twenty seventeen, IceCube traced one high-energy neutrino back to a giant black hole in a galaxy billions of light-years away.
segments.headline: From a distant galaxy

segments.text: That's the end of season four. Next stop: The Hubble Space Telescope. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
